decision: No blocking issue found. This is a platform-selection repair for explicit targets already declared incompatible with the selected Windows/MSVC platform, not a change to compatible lint gates. Actual Windows CI remains required.
source_findings: The full diff is three added lines: two explanatory comments and one bazel_clippy_args append inside the existing RUNNER_OS == Windows branch. The existing MSVC target and host-platform flags are unchanged.

defs.bzl defines WINDOWS_GNULLVM_ONLY as compatible only for the GNULLVM ABI and applies it to generated manual windows-cross-bin rust_test targets. The log identifies all 156 as explicitly incompatible with the actual MSVC target platform.

The Agentd qualification test uses _COGNITIVE_E2E_COMPATIBILITY, with Linux/macOS allowed and all other platforms incompatible. Its UnixProcessDriver/socket rationale is present in the original source.

The target discovery script, entire returned target roster, all compatibility declarations, --config=clippy, Rust sources and target action definitions are unchanged. No allow/ignore lint flag, continue-on-error or successful-exit override is added.
Non-Windows clippy invocation is unchanged. Windows test shards already use the same explicit-incompatibility selection flag.

Existing compatible target actions retain normal failure propagation. No claim is made that the old MSVC invocation ever provided usable GNULLVM coverage; declared ABI-incompatible targets cannot be validated by that platform.

primary_semantics_source.summary: Bazel distinguishes incompatible targets reached by patterns from those explicitly named. The latter normally fail selection; skip_incompatible_explicit_targets makes them skip according to the already-defined target constraints.

validation_scope: This reviewer ran no native Rust, Windows or repository Bazel build.

The separate small Bazel probe attempt01 (profiler crash) and attempt02 (registry certificate failure) were present and failed for environment reasons; they are not counted as passed semantic tests in this receipt.
Source-owned subsequent proof runs, if any, require their own actual receipts.
macOS OOM, other native failures and scientific quality/efficiency gates are outside this three-line repair and remain unchanged.
